A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LongSpec research. All 19 pages of v1 and 23 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, support reliable comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original decoding-speed, token-acceptance, ablation, AIME24 reasoning, and throughput measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds EAGLE benchmark results and measurements stratified by prefill length in Appendices F–G.

M1.justification: The 512-token sliding-window draft architecture, target KV-cache reuse, shared embedding/output weights, Anchor-Offset Indices, flash noisy training, and Hybrid Tree Attention are retained. Revised explanations and attention terminology do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use SlimPajama-6B, Prolong-64k, and the self-built SFT data, and evaluate GovReport, QMSum, Multi-News, LCC, RepoBench-P, and AIME24. The new prefill analysis stratifies retained GovReport coverage rather than introducing another task or domain.

E2.justification: Appendix F/Table 3 adds EAGLE as an end-to-end benchmark comparator across five datasets with Vicuna-7B, LongChat-7B, and LLaMA-3.1-8B. v1 compared an EAGLE implementation only in the latency breakdown. The existing HuggingFace, Flash-Decoding, and MagicDec comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The added EAGLE comparison specifies Anchor-Offset training, HuggingFace attention, and T = 0. Appendix G introduces six prefill-length bins from 0–5k through 25–32k with component timings. Previously reported training budgets, metrics, temperatures, and inference hardware are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix G/Table 4 adds a focused sensitivity analysis testing how LongChat-7B acceptance, decoding speed, and component latency vary with GovReport prefill length. Existing Anchor-Offset ablations, attention timing, batch-size analysis, and all four case-study outputs are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix H newly states that all reported results have zero error bars across runs because evaluation is deterministic with fixed inputs. v1 contains no equivalent statement. No run counts, seeds, or uncertainty-estimation procedure accompany this disclosure, and additional runs are not established.

E6.justification: Tables 3–4 substantially extend comparative and scaling results. Newly reported EAGLE speed on Vicuna-7B/GovReport is 33.43 tokens/s versus LongSpec's retained 102.23; the prefill analysis reports 116.65 tokens/s at 0–5k and 103.68 at 25–32k. Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–7 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: The attention-aggregation proposition and proof, error-bound theorem, mathematical definitions, assumptions, and supporting lemmas are substantively identical. Their relocation, regrouping, and changed cross-references do not introduce new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: v2's introduction adds an up-to-7× HuggingFace speedup headline and replaces v1's 4.1× attention-speedup statement against Medusa with approximately 75% latency reduction against HuggingFace. The three technical contributions, lossless behavior, and 3.26× Flash-baseline/2.25× AIME24 claims retain their meaning.

C2.justification: Appendix B expands the mechanism explanation for how shared KV representations align draft and target predictions. Appendix G interprets stable acceptance across prefill lengths as stable drafting quality. Appendix H newly states the decoder-only Transformer restriction and incompatibility with architectures such as RNNs.

D1.justification: v2 identifies flash_attn_with_kvcache as the attention API, documents the EAGLE adaptation, and identifies LongChat-7B as the model used for the retained cases. Existing hardware, precision, optimizer, learning rates, beam widths, and code-access information remain; training details are partly relocated to Appendix E.

R1.justification: The positioning expands substantially through a new appendix on lossy speculative decoding, discussing speculative cascading, MTAD, judge decoding, RSD, RAPID, and TokenSwift, while relocating BiLD into that discussion. Section 2 also adds QuantSpec and Swift, broadening the comparison with earlier approaches.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, with numbered challenges and contributions and stronger organization around lossless acceleration. Terminology and methodological explanations are revised throughout. Appendices are reorganized, including consolidation of notation, theory, and supporting lemmas and relocation of experimental details.

P2.justification: v2 adds a context-length comparison figure and Tables 3–4, merges and redraws the previous architecture and attention diagrams into Figure 2, and restyles Figure 3. Several retained plots are resized or relocated, and the unchanged case displays are reordered and redistributed across pages.

improvement.justification: The added EAGLE benchmark comparison and prefill-length analysis strengthen the empirical support available in v1. The KV-cache explanation and explicit architecture limitation also improve clarity and scope. These provide a modest net gain, tempered by the new blanket zero-error-bar assertion without supporting run counts or an estimation procedure.
